the-hermit.name: The Hermit
the-hermit.meaning: This card symbolizes inner exploration, solitary reflection, and the inner light. It indicates a need to step away from external noise and take time to find your own truth. It represents a stage of self-awareness where you trust your own wisdom over others' advice or outside validation. Now is the time to spend time alone and quietly seek answers within; the light will reveal itself.
the-hermit.sym_person: An old man wearing a long gray cloak stands alone atop a mountain peak
the-hermit.sym_symbol: A lantern containing starlight, a staff, a snow-covered mountain peak
the-hermit.sym_bg: A dark sky and an isolated mountain summit
the-hermit.upright: The Hermit signifies a time of stepping back from crowded spaces to climb a mountain path alone. The small starlight within the old man's lantern isn't flashy, but it's enough to illuminate the ground beneath his feet even on a dark, snow-covered peak. The answer you need right now is likely to emerge gradually not from someone else's advice or a trendy solution, but through the process of retracing the path you've already walked. Like the old man's slow steps as he leans on his staff, the key to this period is maintaining your own pace, one step at a time, without rushing. It may feel like loneliness, but in truth, you've been given a rare opportunity to look at yourself clearly.
the-hermit.reversed: The reversed Hermit shows that time spent alone is turning into isolation rather than reflection. Just as the lantern's light grows dim, you may become trapped in your own thoughts and lose the ability to see your situation objectively, or conversely, you might escape into meaningless noise because you can't bear being alone. Two opposite extremes can appear together: pushing away others' advice too forcefully, or losing your own voice and being swayed entirely by what others say. Now is the time to re-examine the balance between silence and connection.
the-hermit.love: In love, the Hermit may signal a need to understand yourself before focusing on the relationship. For those who are single, this could mean a period of concentrating on yourself rather than rushing to find a new connection. For those in a relationship, it may mean that both partners need a bit of distance and personal space. This distance isn't a sign of breaking up, but more like a brief pause to help each person sort out their inner world, ultimately moving toward a healthier relationship.
the-hermit.career: In work or career matters, this card suggests quietly checking your own direction without being swayed by others' pace or evaluations. Work that involves quietly building skills or diving deep into research, planning, or analysis alone may align well with the current flow, more so than flashy achievements. Even if your position feels isolated, like standing atop a snow-covered peak, the insight you gain there will help you make clearer decisions later on.
the-hermit.money: When it comes to money matters, the Hermit suggests taking time to calmly examine your financial situation rather than following impulsive spending or someone else's investment advice. Just as a single lantern illuminates only the ground beneath your feet, a small check to accurately grasp the resources you currently have comes before grand plans. When you make judgments based on your own standards without rushing, problems or opportunities that were previously unnoticed may become clearer.
the-hermit.advice: Consider stepping away from others for a while and spending time alone. In that silence, if you listen to what your heart is saying, you may discover that the answer you need was already within you. A single small light is enough to take the next step, so don't rush—trust your own pace.

the-lovers.name: The Lovers
the-lovers.meaning: This card symbolizes choice, alignment of values, and true partnership. It represents not mere emotional attraction but a deep connection of values and standing at a crossroads of an important decision. It marks a moment when inner truth and outer choice must align, and since the decision made now shapes the direction of life, you are invited to ask what you truly desire.
the-lovers.sym_person: A man and woman standing in the Garden of Eden, with an angel bestowing a blessing
the-lovers.sym_symbol: The tree of knowledge with a serpent wrapped around it, a flaming tree, and an angel above the clouds
the-lovers.sym_bg: A paradise-like scene bathed in bright, warm light
the-lovers.upright: The Lovers card opens with two people standing face to face in the middle of paradise, while above them an angel quietly bestows a blessing. This is not simply the joy of meeting someone, but the moment when two different beings confirm their sincere feelings toward each other and decide to move forward in one direction. The tree of knowledge with the serpent wrapped around it shows that temptation or the easy option still exists, but the real question is whether you will follow that temptation or the values you truly believe in. Right now, you may be facing two paths that look similar on the surface but lead to entirely different outcomes, and this card tells you to listen to your inner truth rather than your emotions at this crossroads. Ultimately, the warm light in this scene suggests that true harmony comes not from calculated reasoning but from following the honest answer found deep in your heart.
the-lovers.reversed: When the Lovers card appears reversed, it can indicate that the balance between two beings has broken down, pointing to a relationship or choice that has tilted to one side. It may also mean that although you appear to be together on the surface, your heart is drawn elsewhere, or that as you face an important decision, your gaze keeps drifting toward immediate temptations or the easier path. This is a time when the serpent on the tree of knowledge becomes especially vivid, so it's worth examining whether there's an inner conflict you're knowingly pretending not to notice. Rather than rushing to a conclusion now, it may be more important to honestly face what you've been avoiding.
the-lovers.love: In love, this card shows a flow in which two people confirm each other's values and seriously align their hearts. You may be standing at an important crossroads that requires deciding whether to be together, going beyond mere excitement, and that choice begins with honest conversation. If you're already in a relationship, this may be a time when revealing your true feelings to each other without holding back builds deeper trust.
the-lovers.career: In work or career matters, this can indicate a moment of weighing two options, or needing to align direction with someone you'll be working with. The standard for your decision should be what values truly matter to you, rather than conditions or terms on paper. When entering into collaboration or partnership, the process of checking how well your beliefs align with the other person's may greatly determine your future satisfaction.
the-lovers.money: In financial matters, this can be read as a message to choose according to your own values rather than simple profit. A tempting offer right in front of you may look as alluring as the forbidden fruit, but you need the prudence to consider whether it truly suits your direction. If it's a financial decision made together with someone else, such as a partnership or joint investment, how well your values align with theirs can greatly affect the quality of the outcome.
the-lovers.advice: Now is the time to honestly look at what your heart truly wants, rather than the answer calculated in your head. Don't run from the crossroads before you; accept that this choice will shape your future direction. If this is a decision made together with someone, honest conversation rather than silence will open a better path.

the-magician.name: The Magician
the-magician.meaning: This card symbolizes the ability to create reality through will and skill. The Magician connects heaven (the spiritual world) and earth (the material world), masterfully commanding all four elements. All the necessary tools are already in hand, along with the capacity to use them to achieve one's goals. Now is the time to clarify your intention and take action immediately.
the-magician.sym_person: A man standing with one hand pointing to the sky and the other to the earth
the-magician.sym_symbol: An infinity symbol (∞) above his head, and the four tools—Wands, Cups, Swords, and Pentacles—laid out on a table before him
the-magician.sym_bg: A garden blooming with red roses and white lilies
the-magician.upright: With Wands, Cups, Swords, and Pentacles all arranged on the table, this figure shows a state where the necessary resources are already at hand. The posture of one hand reaching toward the sky and the other toward the earth represents the moment when thought and action become one—where the idea in the mind connects directly to movement in the world. The infinity symbol above his head tells us this connection isn't a one-time event but an ability that can be drawn upon again and again. Right now, ideas, connections, skills, and time may already be scattered around you, and this card is telling you to gather them together and take the first step. Like the red roses and white lilies blooming side by side, when passion and pure intention exist together, the key to creating momentum lies in starting with whatever small action you can take now, rather than worrying over the outcome. What matters isn't whether you have talent, but whether you have the will to actually put what you already possess into use.
the-magician.reversed: The tools remain on the table, but the hands aren't moving—this represents stagnation, having the ability but failing to use it. This often appears when there's a lack of confidence, a habit of endless planning without action, or when energy is scattered in different directions due to an unclear purpose. Sometimes it shows up as a gap between words and actions, or even as the temptation to use one's talents to deceive others. This may be a time to step back from grand plans and instead re-examine what's already in hand, realigning your direction.
the-magician.love: This is a time when you can actively use your charm and communication skills within a relationship—taking the initiative or expressing your feelings openly can create a positive flow. Since the understanding and emotion needed between you are already in place, taking that step forward without hesitation can become the turning point that moves the relationship ahead. Reversed, it may suggest that words are outpacing actions, or that an attempt to control the other person is destabilizing the relationship—sincere communication should come first.
the-magician.career: This card shows that you already have the strength to turn your abilities and ideas into concrete results in your current work. It's a good time to propose a new project or demonstrate your skills—rather than hesitating, it's better to set a concrete plan and act on it right away. Reversed, it may be worth checking yourself realistically so you don't miss your timing through excessive preparation, or fall into the trap of overselling your abilities.
the-magician.money: This card suggests that you already have the ideas or means to earn money, and putting them into action could lead to real, tangible results. It's a favorable time for managing assets or exercising creativity to build new sources of income, so moving from planning to execution is key. Reversed, be cautious of speculative decisions driven by overconfidence, or hasty choices made without sufficient information.
the-magician.advice: Everything you need to achieve what you want is already on the table—rather than waiting for more perfect conditions, try making use of what's already in your hands. Like the hand pointing to the sky and the hand pointing to the earth, intention only becomes reality when thought and action are joined as one. Remember that a single small step can open the door to the next possibility, and take that first step forward.

wheel-of-fortune.name: Wheel of Fortune
wheel-of-fortune.meaning: This card symbolizes the cycles of destiny, unpredictable change, and new phases of life. It reflects the cosmic law that everything turns and returns—whatever your current situation, good or bad, it will not last forever. You must learn to read the timing and flow, and ride the wave of change as it comes. Luck and opportunity are near, so meet them with a prepared mind.
wheel-of-fortune.sym_symbol: A composite wheel made of an outer rim, inner rim, and central hub; the caduceus of Hermes; the Sphinx; Anubis
wheel-of-fortune.sym_bg: A sky above the clouds, with winged creatures in the four corners
wheel-of-fortune.upright: The Wheel of Fortune reveals that life never stays still but keeps turning endlessly. Just as the outer rim, inner rim, and central hub move together in sync, the visible circumstances of your life and the hidden currents beneath them are interconnected—when one moves, the whole turns with it. Like the winged creatures guarding each corner, there is also a suggestion that some unshakable axis exists at the center, even amid the whirlwind of change. If you've felt stuck lately, this is a sign that a new phase is about to open; if things have been going well, it's time to accept that flow with humility rather than taking it for granted. As the caduceus of Hermes suggests, the message and the opportunity have already arrived—only those who are prepared will notice it and seize the moment.
wheel-of-fortune.reversed: Reversed, the Wheel of Fortune suggests that the flow of events may be moving against your wishes, or that change is being delayed. Just as the Sphinx and Anubis hold their positions above and below the wheel, what appears stagnant on the surface may already be shifting beneath it. This card can also appear reversed when you resist change yourself, clinging to what's familiar and trying to force the flow to stop. What remains unchanged, however, is the fact that your current difficulties will not last forever—so instead of rushing, it helps to sense when the flow will open again.
wheel-of-fortune.love: This may be a time when the flow of your relationship reaches an unexpected turning point. If a relationship has been stagnant for a long while, a small action from someone could shift its course entirely; if you're meeting someone new, a chance encounter at just the right timing could bring you together. Just remember that relationships always move in cycles, so rather than placing too much weight on whether things seem good or bad right now, it's better to let yourself flow naturally with the current.
wheel-of-fortune.career: This card suggests that an unexpected opportunity or turning point may arrive for a career that has felt stuck. Things could shift suddenly due to outside factors—a promotion, a job change, a new project—so it's worth staying more alert than usual and keeping an eye on information coming your way. Even if things aren't going well right now, remember that this phase won't last forever, and it helps to prepare for the next turn of the cycle.
wheel-of-fortune.money: This card hints that your financial situation may move in a direction that's hard to predict. Sudden income or expenses, or fluctuations in investments, may appear, so it's wise to carefully observe the flow before making any major decisions. When a good flow comes your way, accept it with gratitude, but stay balanced by not assuming it will last forever—prepare instead for the next turn of the cycle.
wheel-of-fortune.advice: Accept that your current situation, whether good or bad, is not the whole story. If signs of change appear, it's wiser to prepare to ride that flow than to fear it. The wheel turns on its own, but keeping your balance upon it is ultimately up to you.

the-high-priestess.name: The High Priestess
the-high-priestess.meaning: This card symbolizes hidden secrets not yet revealed and deep inner wisdom. It represents truth beyond what is visible, intuition, and the realm of the subconscious. Now is a time to quietly observe rather than act outwardly, and to listen closely to your inner voice. There is information that has not yet come to light, so rather than rushing, wait for the right time.
the-high-priestess.sym_person: A woman sitting between two pillars with a transcendent expression
the-high-priestess.sym_symbol: Two pillars (B and J), a crown of the moon, a Torah scroll, a veil patterned with pomegranates
the-high-priestess.sym_bg: A mysterious space bathed in moonlight
the-high-priestess.upright: The High Priestess sits at the midpoint between the black pillar and the white pillar, leaning toward neither side. This shows that you are now standing before a matter that cannot be simply divided into good and evil, yes and no. The half-unrolled Torah scroll on her lap means that not everything has been read yet, and the truth hidden behind the pomegranate-patterned veil will not open simply because you reach for it impatiently. What is needed now is not to gather more visible information through action, but to quietly focus on an inner sense that, like moonlight, is faint yet clear. This is a time to notice what you already know deep in your heart, rather than rushing to reach a conclusion.
the-high-priestess.reversed: Reversed, the High Priestess shows the veil trembling or slightly pulled aside, indicating that what was hidden has become distorted, or that suppressed intuition is being ignored. You may be so swayed by outside noise or others' opinions that you yourself become confused about what you truly feel. Or, on the contrary, you may be so trapped in secrecy and silence that you keep putting off conversations that need to happen. Now is a time to examine whether you are forcibly ignoring your own intuition, or conversely, carrying everything alone without sharing it.
the-high-priestess.love: There is a strong possibility that feelings not yet expressed, or a true heart not yet spoken, exist within the relationship. If you pay more attention to the subtle signals in expressions and attitudes rather than words, you may gradually come to see where the relationship is heading. Rather than rushing to confess or demand a definite answer, giving each other time for true feelings to naturally surface may benefit the relationship.
the-high-priestess.career: There may be information or variables not yet visible on the surface in the work or relationships currently underway, so it is more advantageous to observe the situation a little longer rather than rushing to a decision. In meetings or negotiations, the sense of reading clues from unspoken atmosphere, a colleague's tone, or silence may play an important role. Rather than showing off outwardly, quietly building skill and preparation may lead to better results in the long run.
the-high-priestess.money: Regarding spending or investment, not all information may be transparently disclosed yet, so if your intuition tells you something feels off, it is wise to look into it further before deciding. This is a time that calls for caution—trying to grasp the hidden conditions or undercurrents rather than just the numbers in front of you. Rather than making a major decision right away, quietly gathering information and waiting for the right time may be the more financially stable choice.
the-high-priestess.advice: Now is a time to sit quietly and listen to the voice within, rather than going out to search for answers. Don't try to understand everything at once—accept that, like a scroll not yet fully unrolled, some things will only reveal themselves with time. Don't take the signals from your intuition lightly; take time to ask yourself what they are trying to tell you.

the-chariot.name: The Chariot
the-chariot.meaning: This card symbolizes willpower, focus, and victory. It represents the ability to control opposing forces and move forward toward a goal. What's needed is the determination to overcome inner conflict and gather your energy in a single direction. This is a time to trust your own will, unshaken by external obstacles, and press onward.
the-chariot.sym_person: An armored warrior stands in a chariot, controlling two sphinxes
the-chariot.sym_symbol: Black and white sphinxes, a canopy engraved with stars, crescent moon shoulder emblems
the-chariot.sym_bg: A triumphant scene with a river and city left behind
the-chariot.upright: The Chariot depicts a figure using sheer will to coordinate a black sphinx and a white sphinx, each pulling in a different direction, and drive them forward together. This represents the ability not to forcefully erase the conflicting impulses or desires within yourself, or the opposing circumstances surrounding you, but rather to guide them all in one unified direction. The armor symbolizes the solid protection you maintain against outside scrutiny or pressure, while the star-engraved canopy represents a cool, clear perspective fixed on your goal, undistracted by emotion. This is a sign that now is not the time to remain indecisive, but rather a period to gather your scattered energy into one and break through the challenge ahead head-on. If you've drawn this card, the power to take control of the situation is already within you—all that remains is to trust it and put it into action.
the-chariot.reversed: The reversed Chariot resembles a scene where the sphinxes pull in different directions, causing the chariot to spin in place without moving forward. It points to a loss of direction, or a state where you have the motivation but can't decide what to focus on first. At times, excessive self-confidence or impatience may actually be creating friction with those around you, blocking your progress. In such moments, it may help to pause and examine what you're really trying to control, and which parts of yourself are in conflict.
the-chariot.love: This may be a time when you feel the urge to take the lead in a relationship and express your feelings clearly, suggesting the need to resolve any hesitation and commit to moving in one direction. However, rather than trying to drag your partner along by force like the sphinxes, it's important to find balance by acknowledging that you each move at your own emotional pace while still leading together. If you're dealing with unrequited love or conflict, clearly defining your own stance without being swept up by emotion could become a turning point in the relationship.
the-chariot.career: This card signifies a period when you have the strength to actively move toward your goals and maintain your own pace even amid competition. It suggests the possibility of good results in situations requiring focus and drive, such as projects, exams, or negotiations. However, if you don't clearly set priorities among different tasks or roles, your energy may become scattered—so it's important to concentrate your efforts on the one thing that matters most right now.
the-chariot.money: This is a period when your resolve to set financial goals and act on them grows stronger, with momentum to decisively follow through on planned expenses or investments. Rather than wavering between different financial options, it's advantageous to set priorities and focus your resources in one direction. However, if confidence turns to overconfidence, it could lead to reckless decisions, so maintaining balance without losing control is important.
the-chariot.advice: Now is the time to practice aligning the conflicting voices within you in one direction, rather than suppressing them. Instead of being swayed by outside circumstances, it helps to keep your own goal at the center and make a firm, resolute move forward when the moment calls for it. Prepare to protect yourself like armor, but rather than pushing through with sheer force, try advancing toward where you want to be through balanced control.

the-hierophant.name: The Hierophant
the-hierophant.meaning: Represents tradition, institutions, and collective belief systems. It signifies the transmission of knowledge between teacher and student, and the value of established norms and customs. This is a time to seek a sense of belonging to community and spiritual guidance, looking for answers within tried-and-true methods and traditional wisdom.
the-hierophant.sym_person: A high priest making a gesture of blessing before two followers
the-hierophant.sym_symbol: The papal triple crown, two crossed keys, white lilies and red roses
the-hierophant.sym_bg: The interior of a cathedral with two pillars
the-hierophant.upright: The Hierophant shows a priest seated between two pillars, bestowing a blessing upon his followers, signaling that this is a time to seek answers within proven systems and tradition rather than relying solely on personal intuition. The two crossed keys in his hands symbolize the wisdom to unlock both the worldly and spiritual realms, suggesting that this knowledge is not something achieved alone, but rather passed down through a mentor or a long-established system. The white lily and red rose at his feet show that pure faith and practical action must exist in harmony, hinting at the need for a balanced attitude rather than chasing ideals alone or following rules alone. If this card appears, it may open up a flow toward socially recognized processes such as marriage, joining a company, or obtaining a certification, or toward learning within a religious, philosophical, or educational institution. Rather than forging a new path, trusting in existing good systems and the advice of experienced people may be the more stable choice for now.
the-hierophant.reversed: When the Hierophant appears reversed, it may be a time when resistance to established norms or authority, or skepticism toward formal procedures, begins to surface. Just as the authority of the triple-crowned figure wavers, you may feel that the ways of a teacher, institution, or organization you once trusted no longer fit you. This isn't necessarily a bad sign—it could be read as a signal to step outside rigid conventions and build your own belief system instead. However, disregarding existing order entirely could lead to isolation or unnecessary friction, so you'll need to discern for yourself what to preserve and what to change.
the-hierophant.love: This may be a time when the desire for a socially stable relationship framework, such as a traditional courtship or marriage, grows stronger, with a wish to formalize the relationship with your partner coming to the surface. Like the two followers standing side by side before the priest, shared values, family background, or the approval of those around you may play an important role in the relationship. However, to avoid getting caught up in formality and appearances at the expense of genuine feeling, it's worth looking beyond the outward shape of the relationship to the texture of the hearts involved.
the-hierophant.career: This indicates a flow of settling into a stable position while respecting organizational rules, procedures, and hierarchy, and it may be a favorable time to pass formal verification processes such as certifications, degrees, or promotion reviews. Advice from an experienced supervisor or mentor could be genuinely helpful, so it's worth adopting a learning attitude rather than relying solely on your own judgment. Rather than starting a business or attempting something unconventional, steadily building your career within an existing system may lead to more solid results at this stage.
the-hierophant.money: In financial matters, following the advice of an established institution or professional may be the safer choice, and this is a time better suited to stable, conventional management rather than new or unfamiliar investments. Matters requiring careful attention to form and procedure, such as contracts, regulations, or tax issues, may arise, so it's important not to neglect your paperwork. Rather than overextending, sticking to your existing financial principles may provide greater stability in the long run.
the-hierophant.advice: Now is a time to listen to proven wisdom and the advice of experienced people rather than insisting on doing things your own way. Like standing between two pillars, maintaining balance among differing values while walking a steady path can be helpful. Even if tradition and convention feel restrictive, taking a moment to look deeply into the meaning behind them may offer a clue to resolving your current situation.

the-fool.name: The Fool
the-fool.meaning: This card symbolizes new beginnings and a pure sense of adventure. It represents the energy of taking a first step into the unknown from a blank slate, with nothing yet determined. It holds both the freshness of starting without experience and the possibility of recklessness that comes with it. You are on the verge of opening a new chapter right now, and this is a time to trust your intuition and move forward rather than overanalyzing.
the-fool.sym_person: A young man walking toward the sky at the edge of a cliff, followed by a white dog
the-fool.sym_symbol: A white rose (purity), a small knapsack, a staff
the-fool.sym_bg: A bright sky and snow-capped mountain peaks
the-fool.upright: The Fool card, through the image of a figure standing at the edge of a cliff yet gazing at the sky with curiosity rather than fear, shows a mindset willing to take the first step even when the outcome cannot be predicted. The small knapsack on his back carries the message that you can set out with only the bare essentials, suggesting a way of learning as you go rather than moving only after perfecting your plan. The white rose signifies that the journey springs from pure motives, and the white dog following behind can be read as a symbol that instinct or intuition will watch over you. The choice in front of you right now is likely an unfamiliar path rather than a familiar one, and this may be a time when it's fine to lean toward excitement rather than the tension that unfamiliarity brings. Still, as the cliff setting suggests, you also need the flexibility to check your footing step by step rather than charging ahead without any sense of direction.
the-fool.reversed: The reversed Fool can signal a warning against leaping without preparation, or conversely, a state of endlessly hesitating and postponing that first step. It resembles the figure freezing up, now overly conscious of what's beneath his feet, rather than walking along the cliff's edge without looking down. If there's been a pattern of repeated reckless decisions, this may be a point where you face the consequences again; or conversely, you might be missing opportunities altogether by chasing only safety. What's needed now isn't to stop completely, but to take time to examine for yourself where the balance has broken down.
the-fool.love: In matters of love, the Fool shows a flow where a new encounter begins in an unexpected place, or fresh energy enters an existing relationship. It can also be a time when your desire grows to follow genuine affection and excitement as they are, rather than calculating or measuring the other person. However, the speed of emotion may outpace the depth of the relationship, so while keeping that purity intact, it helps to enjoy the process of getting to know each other.
the-fool.career: For questions about career or work, this card connects to a flow of challenging yourself in a new field or taking on an unfamiliar project that departs from your usual way of working. Having little experience or a short career history may actually work in your favor, bringing an unbiased perspective that leads to unexpectedly good results. However, a small knapsack also means your preparation isn't perfect, so it's wise to also check the minimum necessary information and assess the risks.
the-fool.money: Financially, this can be interpreted as a flow of trying a new source of income or encountering an unexpected expense or investment opportunity. This may be a period when impulsive decisions outpace planning, so if a large sum is involved, you'll need the same caution as walking along the edge of a cliff, checking one step ahead. Starting with small attempts to build a feel for things can help reduce the risk of excessive loss.
the-fool.advice: Right now, rather than trying to calculate every variable before moving, an attitude of taking one step and learning as you go suits you better. Accepting that perfect preparation never really exists in the first place can lighten your heart considerably. Still, so that this step doesn't drift into recklessness, please try to find balance between your own instincts and a minimal sense of realism.

the-empress.name: The Empress
the-empress.meaning: A card of abundance, creativity, and the embodiment of maternal love. It symbolizes the bounty of nature and the flourishing of life, representing a time when artistic creativity and sensual pleasure come into bloom. Like the process of planting a seed and watching it bear fruit, the energy of nurturing and growth overflows. It is a time to exercise your ability to enrich both yourself and others.
the-empress.sym_person: A woman with an air of abundance sits in a comfortable chair
the-empress.sym_symbol: A crown of twelve stars, a dress patterned with pomegranates, a shield bearing the symbol of Venus, fields of wheat and fruit
the-empress.sym_bg: A lush forest and a flowing waterfall
the-empress.upright: The Empress carries the power to make everything she touches grow. The lush forest and the cascading waterfall show nature's rhythm of flowing and multiplying on its own, without being forced—a sign that a similar cycle is beginning around you as well. The pomegranate-patterned dress, the wheat fields, and the ripened fruit represent a stage where long-accumulated effort, relationships, or ideas are finally turning into visible results. The crown set with twelve stars symbolizes a harmony of sense, intuition, and creativity working together to guide oneself, while her relaxed posture represents the ease with which people and resources naturally gather around her, without strain. During this time, it is favorable to direct your energy toward nurturing both yourself and those around you through care, patience, and sensory enjoyment.
the-empress.reversed: When the Empress appears reversed, it can point to a blockage in the flow of abundance, or conversely, to a state of being overwhelmed and depleted by too much of it. It may be time to reflect on whether you have lost yourself through excessive caretaking, or whether you have been giving too much for the sake of others' growth. Even with creative energy present, you might feel frustration or stagnation because it isn't translating into tangible results, and you may have neglected to care for your body and senses. Just as an unattended forest becomes overrun with weeds rather than flourishing, this card quietly warns that abundance without direction can become a burden instead.
the-empress.love: This card shows a flow in which comfort and warmth naturally grow within a relationship, with mutual care deepening and stabilizing the bond over time. In an existing relationship, it may be a period when sensual intimacy and emotional connection ripen together, and if you're meeting someone new, you are likely coming across as comfortably appealing to them. However, it's worth checking occasionally whether your tendency to care for and protect the other person might be hindering their independence.
the-empress.career: At work, this is a favorable flow for ideas to grow into concrete results, and projects you've been preparing may start to bear fruit. You may particularly shine in roles involving collaboration, mentoring, or caring for a team, and if your field calls for creativity and aesthetic sense, you're likely to receive good recognition. However, rather than taking everything on yourself, adopting an attitude of sharing abundance by making use of the resources around you will lead to greater growth in the long run.
the-empress.money: Financially, this is a time when returns come gradually in proportion to the seeds you've planted, favoring steady accumulation and a stable income structure over sudden windfalls. You may find yourself inclined to spend money on things that enrich your life and care for yourself, which can be a satisfying choice as long as it stays within reasonable limits. However, it's wise to maintain balance so that the feeling of abundance doesn't lead to unplanned overspending.
the-empress.advice: Now is a time to trust the pace at which the seed grows, rather than rushing toward results. Listen to the signals your senses and body are sending you, and don't push self-care to the bottom of your priority list. Remember that abundance grows larger when it is shared—nurturing the people and resources around you generously will ultimately come back to benefit you as well.

the-emperor.name: The Emperor
the-emperor.meaning: This card symbolizes authority, order, structure, and stability. It carries the energy of a leader who sets rules and boundaries while taking responsibility. Decision-making grounded in logic and principle, along with a systematic approach, is needed now. To achieve your goals on solid ground, you must cultivate discipline and consistency.
the-emperor.sym_person: A powerful man in armor sits upon a high throne
the-emperor.sym_symbol: A throne adorned with ram's heads, a scepter and orb, a red cloak
the-emperor.sym_bg: A rugged wilderness surrounded by jagged mountains
the-emperor.upright: Seated on a throne in the middle of the wilderness, the Emperor is a figure who has established order not on soft ground but atop rugged mountains. This tells you that the situation you're facing now must be handled not with emotion or impulse, but with clear structure and principle. The ram's head ornaments symbolize a stubborn, persistent drive to execute, while the scepter and orb in his hands represent the ability to define the scope of what you can control. As the red cloak suggests, beneath his cold, composed exterior lies a burning sense of responsibility for what must be protected. Now is the time to establish rules, draw clear boundaries, and lead the situation with unwavering standards.
the-emperor.reversed: The reversed Emperor indicates that the throne is shaking, or the armor has become too heavy to bear. Legitimate authority may have degenerated into stubbornness or a need for control, causing rigidity that creates friction in your relationships with others. Alternatively, the standards themselves may have collapsed, leading to inconsistent decisions or avoidance of responsibility. Now is the time to reexamine who your authority actually serves, rather than forcing it into place.
the-emperor.love: This is a period when the desire for stability and commitment within a relationship grows stronger, and you may be expecting clear promises or direction from your partner. However, like the rigid posture upon the throne, clinging too tightly to principle alone can block the flow of emotional exchange, so flexibility is also needed. When the desire to guide the relationship is balanced with respect for your partner, this card becomes a solid foundation of support.
the-emperor.career: A moment is approaching where you'll need to exercise leadership or establish a clear structure within an organization or project. Even in difficult circumstances as rugged as jagged mountains, organizing rules and procedures creates an unshakable foundation to move forward on. However, excessive control or unilateral decisions can hinder cooperation from those around you—authority built on trust is what lasts.
the-emperor.money: In financial matters, a planned, structured approach is more advantageous now than impulsive decisions. As the scepter and orb symbolize, clearly understanding the scope of resources you have and managing them with discipline within those limits creates stability. If you build a long-term plan and hold to your principles, the foundation you lay now can grow into solid assets.
the-emperor.advice: What's needed now is unwavering principle and the sense of responsibility to uphold it. But make sure this authority serves to steady yourself rather than to suppress others. Order built upon solid ground will ultimately become a protective boundary for both you and those around you.

death.name: Death
death.meaning: This card symbolizes endings and new beginnings, transformation and transition. It represents not physical death, but the complete closing of a chapter. Just as the old must fade away for the new to be born, this is an inevitable process—only by releasing what we cling to can we move forward to the next stage. If you embrace change rather than fear it, a deeper transformation can unfold.
death.sym_person: A skeleton knight in black armor rides forward on a white horse
death.sym_symbol: A black banner bearing a white rose, the white horse, a horizon where the sun sets
death.sym_bg: A river and horizon where dawn is breaking
death.upright: The skeleton knight in black armor does not stop, urging the white horse ever forward. This means that once any emotion, relationship, or habit has run out of life force, no amount of holding on can reverse its course. Like the white rose on the black banner, this card tells us that even death can be a pure and inevitable process. The setting sun beyond the horizon marks the close of an era, but at the same time, the dawn breaking across the river shows that this ending is itself the starting point of the next phase. What you need right now is not resistance, but the courage to honestly acknowledge what has already ended and let it go.
death.reversed: Death reversed shows a state of forcibly clinging to a flow that has already ended. The white horse wants to move forward, but it's as if the reins are being pulled back—a fear of change may be delaying a natural transition. This often manifests as stagnation or inertia, dragging out a relationship or situation that should be concluded, only making things harder for yourself. What's needed now is not pressure to rush the change, but time to look within and understand why you can't let go.
death.love: This suggests that a certain form of your current relationship or feelings may be reaching its natural end. This doesn't necessarily mean separation—it may instead signal that the way you relate to each other, or the stage of the relationship, needs to change completely. When you let go of attachment to old patterns, room opens up for an even deeper and more genuine connection to begin in its place.
death.career: There may be a natural conclusion coming to your current way of working, your role, or the environment you've been part of. Rather than a failure, this can be seen as an inevitable passage toward the next stage, much like the white horse moving forward. The key question is whether you're ready to fully let go of familiar methods and embrace a new direction.
death.money: This can be read as a sign that an old spending habit, a particular income structure, or an investment approach is no longer viable. If there's a financial plan you've been forcing yourself to hold onto, this may be a good opportunity to clear it away and explore a different approach. Even if the current loss or cleanup feels painful, just as dawn breaks, room will open afterward to build a clearer financial foundation.
death.advice: Accepting that something has ended, rather than denying it, will make your next step lighter. Like the white horse's stride, change has already begun, and the more you try to stop it, the more you'll only exhaust yourself. Instead of lingering over the setting sun, try turning your gaze toward the new horizon brightening beyond it.

the-devil.name: The Devil
the-devil.meaning: This card symbolizes being caught up in obsession, addiction, or material desire. It represents beliefs or habits that bind you, but like loosely hung chains, there is actually room for choice. It's a state where fear or desire clouds your vision, calling for the courage to see clearly what is binding you and to break free from those chains.
the-devil.sym_person: A horned devil figure holding two people bound by loose chains
the-devil.sym_symbol: An inverted pentagram, loosely hung chains (which can be removed by the wearers themselves), a torch
the-devil.sym_bg: A dark cave or underground space
the-devil.upright: This scene, set in a dark cave where a horned figure has placed chains around the necks of two people, may signal that you are currently held back by some habit, relationship, or desire. What's interesting is that the chains aren't tightly fastened but hang loosely, showing that you could free yourself if you truly wanted to. Yet people often know this and still choose not to break free, held back by familiarity, comfort, or fear. This may be the time to reflect on whether your current sense of being stuck stems not from outside pressure but from a framework you've built yourself. If a burning desire or obsession, like the torch's flame, is clouding your judgment, you need to pause and honestly face what is really holding you back.
the-devil.reversed: This can indicate movement toward freeing yourself from your chains, or beginning to recognize the true nature of what has bound you. You may have found the will to break away from a long-repeated bad habit or an unhealthy relationship, or you might already be in the process of gradually shedding that burden. However, this isn't complete liberation—old temptations and patterns may still linger, carrying the risk of being pulled back temporarily. The process of breaking free may not go smoothly, so rather than being discouraged by small setbacks, it's important to focus on the fact that you're moving in the right direction.
the-devil.love: This can show a state where partners are excessively dependent on each other, or where one is holding onto the other with feelings closer to obsession than love. What looks like affection on the surface is often actually held together by control and anxiety, so it's worth examining whether this relationship continues because it's truly wanted. Just as the chains are loosely hung, there's still plenty of room to restore a healthy distance or change the dynamic of the relationship, if you choose to.
the-devil.career: This may indicate a situation where your current job is stable but unsatisfying, and you remain stuck simply out of familiarity or fear rather than genuine choice. It's worth checking whether excessive pressure about work or obsession with results is wearing you down. Even if change seems difficult, options do exist, so rather than accepting your current framework as a given, it helps to stay open to other possibilities.
the-devil.money: This is a time to examine whether you're being excessively driven by spending habits or material desires. Spending for instant gratification, debt, or anxiety about money may be clouding your judgment. Fortunately, you still hold the power to control the situation, and simply recognizing emotional spending patterns can be the key to changing the flow.
the-devil.advice: Take another look at just how solid what feels like it's binding you really is. If the chains were forged by fear, you likely already have the strength to break them yourself. Change can begin from honestly facing what the real problem actually is.

the-tower.name: The Tower
the-tower.meaning: This card symbolizes sudden change, collapse, and the disintegration of foundations. It represents a shocking yet necessary purification process in which things built upon false foundations crumble in an instant. Remember that false structures and beliefs must be dismantled before truth can emerge, and that this is a process aimed at creating a better foundation. Even when something frightening occurs, it marks the beginning of true rebuilding.
the-tower.sym_symbol: A tower struck by lightning and engulfed in flames, a crown flying off, lightning bolts, two falling figures
the-tower.sym_bg: A dark, stormy sky and rugged cliffs
the-tower.upright: In this scene, lightning strikes the top of the tower and the crown is hurled into the sky, revealing that the structure once believed to be secure had actually harbored cracks for a long time. A period may arrive when relationships, careers, or belief systems that appeared solid on the surface begin to shake without warning, and the shock felt will be anything but mild. However, this collapse is not a random catastrophe—it is closer to something that had already reached its limit finally breaking free because it could no longer hold. Like the two falling figures, you may be forced to come down from a position and certainty you once held, but waiting at the end of that fall is the freedom of no longer having to stand on falsehood. Frightening as it may be, this moment should be understood not as destruction but as the clearing of ground for rebuilding.
the-tower.reversed: When the Tower appears reversed, it can indicate that you are deliberately ignoring signs of collapse you have already sensed, or forcing yourself to hold up something you know is bound to fall. Rather than bursting out into the open, the shock festers quietly within, and small cracks may accumulate into a larger rupture later on. At times, this may also represent a stage of recovery after a collapse already experienced, or intense resistance to change. In such cases, rather than forcing yourself to endure, it is important to honestly look at what is actually shaking.
the-tower.love: This may be a time when problems long buried within a relationship suddenly surface through an unexpected argument or confession. Rather than signaling the end of the relationship, this can be seen as an opportunity to break down what was built on a false peace and rebuild a more honest foundation. For those who are single, long-held certainties or ideals about themselves may shatter, becoming an opportunity to discover what kind of relationship they truly want.
the-tower.career: In work or career matters, this suggests the possibility of sudden restructuring, a project falling through, or an unexpected decision. The position you currently hold may actually have been standing on unstable ground, and this change may serve to make that fact clear. Though it may feel chaotic for now, this collapse opens room to redesign a more realistic and sustainable foundation for your career afterward.
the-tower.money: In financial matters, unexpected shocks may appear, such as sudden expenses, investment losses, or the collapse of a trusted source of income. This may be the moment when a financial structure built up under strain, or baseless optimism, collides with reality. Rather than being shaken by the immediate loss, it is important to identify what was unstable from the start and use this as an opportunity to rebuild a sturdier financial foundation.
the-tower.advice: If something in your life is currently falling apart, look first at why it is collapsing rather than struggling to hold it together. The shock is brief, but the truth it reveals will make your path forward far clearer. Choosing what to keep and what to rebuild from the rubble is the most realistic way to get through this time.

the-moon.name: The Moon
the-moon.meaning: The Moon symbolizes uncertainty, illusion, and the fears of the subconscious. This is a time when unconscious anxiety and vague fears can cloud judgment, and what you see may not be the whole truth. It's wise to trust your intuition while postponing important decisions until you have clearer information. When you face the source of your fear directly, the illusion lifts and the truth comes into view.
the-moon.sym_symbol: A full moon (with a face), two towers, a dog and a wolf, a crayfish emerging from the water, a winding path
the-moon.upright: The Moon card depicts a state of standing on a misty night road. Far in the distance, a winding path stretches between two towers, but the hazy moonlight alone can't reveal where it leads. The sight of the dog and wolf howling together at the moon represents a psychological state where the familiar and the unfamiliar blend together, making it hard to tell what the real threat actually is. The crayfish quietly emerging from the water hints that emotions or memories long buried beneath the surface of consciousness are gradually rising up—something that can feel frightening, yet also offers a chance to understand yourself more deeply. Rather than rushing to conclusions based only on what's visible right now, this is a time that calls for the patience to wait until the fog clears.
the-moon.reversed: The reversed Moon shows a flow in which the vague anxiety that has weighed on your heart for a long time begins to gradually lift. A moment may arrive where you realize that the fear, once inflated and shapeless in the fog, wasn't actually as big as it seemed. Still, things aren't fully clear yet, so there's a chance that some misunderstanding or distorted information remains. This can also be read as a sign that you're finally ready to face emotions you've been suppressing, rather than continuing to avoid them.
the-moon.love: You may be unsure of your partner's true feelings and letting needless imagination weigh on your heart. Like the winding path, this is a point where emotions on both sides aren't clearly expressed, making misunderstandings easy to build up—so it's best to hold back from assumptions until you've confirmed things through direct conversation. If you're contemplating an unrequited love or the direction of a relationship, it may help to ask yourself whether what you feel is genuine attraction or an illusion born from loneliness.
the-moon.career: This may be a time when the situation at work or in your career path isn't clear enough to make solid plans. Anxiety can easily grow if you're swayed by rumors or uncertain information, so it's safer to hold off on major decisions until you have solid grounds for them. At the same time, this period can be a good opportunity to seriously examine intuitions or uncomfortable signals you've been ignoring.
the-moon.money: Information surrounding your financial situation may be unclear, or you may be suffering from worries that are more exaggerated than reality. If you're facing a decision about an investment or major expense, it's important to rely on concrete data and fact-checking rather than gut feeling alone. This is a good time to calmly check whether you're imagining a crisis that doesn't actually exist, driven by vague anxiety.
the-moon.advice: Don't assume that what you see now is the whole picture—allow yourself some room to wait a little longer until the fog clears. If you look steadily at the fear inside you instead of turning away from it, you may find it's not as big as you thought. Until solid information and time accumulate, it's wise to listen to your intuition while avoiding hasty conclusions.

the-sun.name: The Sun
the-sun.meaning: It symbolizes joy, success, vitality, and clarity. This is a time when darkness lifts and everything comes to light, carrying the energy of embracing life's joy as purely as an inner child. Confidence and optimism overflow, making it an ideal time to accomplish something. Allow yourself to freely express and enjoy this positive energy.
the-sun.sym_person: A child joyfully riding a white horse
the-sun.sym_symbol: A large radiant sun, a wall filled with sunflowers, a banner
the-sun.upright: The enormous sun hanging at the center of the sky means there is nothing left to hide. Situations, relationships, or outcomes that were once unclear now become clear, and this reveals a largely positive direction. Like a child laughing brightly atop a white horse, this is a time when it's alright to fully embrace the achievement and joy of this moment without calculation or doubt. The wall covered in sunflowers symbolizes results that bloom naturally without forced effort, suggesting that this favorable flow is likely to continue without much trouble. Rarely is there a better time than now to show your confidence and move toward what you want.
the-sun.reversed: When the Sun appears reversed, it's less that the brightness disappears entirely and more that it feels temporarily obscured by clouds. Even facing a moment of success or joy, you might lack confidence in yourself, or excessive optimism may be causing you to overlook something important. Your confidence could be tipping into arrogance, or conversely, you might be too withdrawn to fully enjoy the bright outcome as it is. Rather than rushing to force results, it may help to slow down and reexamine the current situation.
the-sun.love: In love, the Sun card represents a relationship where both people are openly honest with each other, with a comfortable and bright energy flowing between you when together. If you're pursuing someone, expressing your feelings is likely to receive a good response; for couples, this can be seen as a time when trust and affection grow even stronger. Showing your genuine, unadorned self within the relationship may actually lead to a better outcome.
the-sun.career: In work or career matters, this suggests that your efforts so far may show up as noticeable achievements, or an opportunity may arise to confidently showcase your strengths. You can expect an especially favorable flow in situations where you need to express yourself, such as presentations, interviews, or negotiations. It's also a favorable time to begin a new project or challenge, so if there's a plan you've been hesitating on, now may be worth acting on it.
the-sun.money: Financially, this card suggests that blocked areas may open up and income or gains could appear in visible, tangible form. This is a time when you can expect positive news in matters with clear outcomes, such as investments or contracts. However, the better the flow, the more important it is to stay attentive and manage well what you've gained.
the-sun.advice: Right now, there's no need to hide or diminish yourself—you can confidently show your true self and your achievements as they are. Like a child laughing atop a horse, focus on the joy and confidence of this moment rather than fear of the outcome. If you trust in this bright flow while keeping a grounded, realistic perspective, this joy can last even longer.

the-star.name: The Star
the-star.meaning: It symbolizes hope, healing, inspiration, and renewal. It carries the energy of peace and fresh expectation that arrives after hardship. It represents an optimistic, healing power that pours abundance into both the inner and outer self. Wounds are mending, and a path toward a brighter future is opening, so it is a time to trust yourself and trust what lies ahead.
the-star.sym_person: A naked woman pours water from two jugs onto the land and into the water
the-star.sym_symbol: One large star and seven smaller stars, two jugs, an ibis bird
the-star.sym_bg: A calm pond and a clear night sky
the-star.upright: Just as starlight becomes visible only after passing through the darkest night, this card speaks of a quiet moment of recovery that comes to someone who has made it through a difficult time. The naked woman pouring water without any protection or disguise suggests that you can now face the world just as you are, with no need to hide or adorn yourself. By pouring water with one hand into the pond and the other onto the earth, she shows a balanced attitude that shares fresh vitality with both inner emotion and outer reality. The one large star surrounded by seven smaller stars offers reassurance that the difficulty you face now is not yours alone, but connected to a larger flow. This is a time to trust in your own recovery rather than rushing for results, and to let your heart rest in the possibilities that are gradually opening up.
the-star.reversed: The reversed Star shows a state in which the light of hope has dimmed and belief in oneself has weakened. Like water from the jugs spilling in the wrong direction, effort and devotion may lose their way and lead instead to emptiness or disappointment. As if the ibis has vanished, inspiration or intuition may be hard to come by, and anxiety and self-doubt may take root in place of trust in the future. However, this is not complete despair—it simply means the starlight is briefly hidden behind clouds, and it may be a sign that instead of pushing yourself harder, you need a pause to regroup.
the-star.love: A time is approaching when you and your partner can be honest with each other without pretense, and wounds that once hurt are slowly healing, giving you room to believe in love again. If you are in unrequited love or in the midst of conflict, watching the natural flow of things rather than rushing for a definite answer may open a more positive direction for the relationship. For those waiting for a new encounter, this suggests a time when your genuine charm can shine without needing to force any outward display.
the-star.career: If your efforts so far have quietly accumulated out of sight, this card shows a flow in which those results begin to gradually surface. New inspiration or direction may come to mind for concerns about your career path that once felt uncertain, so it helps to stay open to the options that draw you intuitively. Rather than rushing toward big achievements, moving forward steadily at your own pace can lead to more stable results in the long run.
the-star.money: Rather than a dramatic change in your financial situation, this indicates a flow in which steady management and patience gradually lead to stability. Just as water spreads evenly from the two jugs, this is a time when balanced allocation and planning help more than reckless spending or speculation. Instead of expecting big gains right away, focusing on recovery and reorganization can make things go more smoothly going forward.
the-star.advice: Now is a time to accept and comfort yourself as you are, rather than pushing yourself harder. Like the stars in the night sky, even if things in front of you aren't fully bright yet, remember that the light of hope already exists within them. When you set aside impatience and respect the pace of your own recovery, the next step will come into clearer view.

justice.name: Justice
justice.meaning: This card symbolizes cause and effect, fairness, and balance. It represents the universal law that every action carries a corresponding consequence. This is a time to evaluate situations objectively and make fair judgments. When facing legal matters or important decisions, choices grounded in truth will lead to just outcomes.
justice.sym_person: A crowned figure holds a scale and a sword while seated between two pillars
justice.sym_symbol: A balanced scale, a double-edged sword, two pillars
justice.sym_bg: A red cloak and purple drapery
justice.upright: Like the figure sitting upright between the two pillars, the Justice card tells you that now is the time to view your situation clearly, without leaning to either side. The scale in hand signals that you should set aside emotion and bias to weigh facts and evidence, while the sword on the other side carries the meaning of bringing that judgment to a clear and decisive close rather than letting it stay clouded. If this card appears, it's worth reflecting on how your recent choices or actions are returning to you, or whether you're approaching the point where they will. If you're signing a contract or making an important decision, prioritizing documentation and facts over emotion may work in your favor. Ultimately, this card shows that things flow smoothly when you apply a fair standard both to yourself and to others.
justice.reversed: When Justice appears reversed, like a scale tipped to one side, it's time to check whether bias or emotion has crept into your judgment. You may need to consider whether you're being treated unfairly, or conversely, whether you yourself are being unfair to someone else. If the matter involves legal issues or contracts, it helps to review the documents again and check for anything overlooked. If you've been avoiding consequences or deferring responsibility, that may be the very thing blocking the flow right now.
justice.love: This is a time to check whether the balance in your relationship has tipped, with one side sacrificing or enduring more than the other. Rather than covering up issues between you two with emotion, addressing them honestly through conversation can bring more clarity to the relationship. If there's something from the past that calls for responsibility or an apology, now may be a good time to bring it to a close.
justice.career: This card suggests the possibility that your efforts and achievements will be fairly recognized going forward. It may work in your favor in situations requiring fair judgment, such as contracts, promotion reviews, or negotiations, so it's wise to prepare your documents and evidence carefully. However, if there has been inaccurate reporting or shortcuts taken, this may also be a time when such things come to light, so maintaining honesty is important.
justice.money: This is a good time to review the balance between your income and expenses, or to handle financial matters that require precision, such as taxes, contracts, or settlements. If there's money you've lent or borrowed in the past, or a settlement that's been postponed, a resolution may be on the horizon. Handling money with transparency and principle can bring both trust and benefit in the long run.
justice.advice: Right now is a moment to rely on facts rather than feelings when making judgments. Reflect on whether your choices have been ones you can stand behind, and find the courage to resolve any responsibility you've been putting off. Fairness may feel like a loss in the moment, but in the end, it will make your position more solid.

the-hanged-man.name: The Hanged Man
the-hanged-man.meaning: This card symbolizes voluntary sacrifice, seeing things from a different perspective, and a temporary pause. It suggests that now is a time to stop what you've been doing and gain a new point of view. Stepping back as a conscious choice, rather than being forced to wait, has value, and letting go and acceptance can actually bring new insight. Instead of resisting, consider what you might learn from this process.
the-hanged-man.sym_person: A man hanging upside down from a tree by one foot, his expression calm and peaceful
the-hanged-man.sym_symbol: A T-shaped tree, a halo around his head, loosely bound hands
the-hanged-man.sym_bg: Green leaves, a calm natural background
the-hanged-man.upright: The Hanged Man hangs upside down, yet his face shows peace rather than pain. This suggests that the current state of suspension may not be a punishment or failure, but a pause he has chosen for himself. The fact that only one foot is bound while his hands hang loose also means he isn't entirely trapped—there's still room to face this situation with a different attitude whenever he chooses. Rather than struggling to produce results right now, this is a time to turn the problem upside down and look at it from a reversed viewpoint, much like the figure's inverted gaze upon the world. The faint halo around his head hints that this period of stillness and patience may eventually lead to a small but meaningful realization.
the-hanged-man.reversed: Reversed, the Hanged Man can represent feeling stuck not by choice but by circumstance beyond your control. Instead of shifting perspective, resistance and impatience toward the situation may grow, leaving you with the sense of spinning in place. Alternatively, it may indicate that you've paused for so long that you're now missing the moment when you should move again. If this card appears reversed, it may be worth asking yourself whether letting go has become an excuse for avoidance.
the-hanged-man.love: Rather than forcing something in your current relationship, it may help to step back for a moment and view the situation from your partner's perspective. Even a stagnant period that feels frustrating can become an opportunity to understand the other person, and that understanding can change the texture of the relationship. If you're single, rather than impatiently chasing a new connection, time spent reflecting on yourself can serve as preparation for the next relationship.
the-hanged-man.career: You may feel that your work is stalled or that you're not moving in the direction you want, but this is less a sign of incompetence and more a signal to reexamine your job or career path from a different angle. Rather than rushing into major decisions like a promotion or a job change, it may help later to consider what you can learn from your current position. Even if results aren't visible right now, the observation and reflection of this period can become an important asset for future choices.
the-hanged-man.money: Rather than making hasty decisions about investments or spending, it may be advantageous to pause and look at the bigger picture again. Even if the lack of immediate returns feels frustrating, it doesn't necessarily mean loss, and it can be seen as a chance to reorganize your financial habits. Rather than acting rashly, it may be safer for now to wait and watch while reviewing other options.
the-hanged-man.advice: If you feel stuck right now, try accepting it not as failure but as an opportunity to shift your perspective. Rather than resisting, take time to quietly look into what this situation is trying to teach you. Just as his hands aren't completely bound, a small shift in mindset can change how you experience this period of stillness.

judgement.name: Judgement
judgement.meaning: Symbolizes resurrection, awakening, and answering an inner call. It represents a state of being ready to leave the past behind and move toward a higher stage of being. It is a transformative process of releasing the old and being reborn as one's true self, a time to respond to the calling that resounds deep within. Answering the inner call without fear opens the door to a new dimension of life.
judgement.sym_symbol: The Archangel Gabriel blowing a trumpet, a red cross flag, figures rising in resurrection from their coffins
judgement.sym_bg: A vast body of water and clouds surrounded by mountains
judgement.upright: Like the figures rising from their coffins at the sound of Archangel Gabriel's trumpet, the Judgement card signals a point where one must take stock of how they have lived and step forward into a new phase. This is not a sudden event, but rather a moment where an awareness that has long been accumulating within finally rises to the surface and can no longer be ignored. As the red cross flag symbolizes, salvation or resurrection is not reserved for those with special qualifications, but is open to anyone willing to acknowledge their life as it is and respond to it. The landscape of water and clouds surrounded by mountains represents the broad perspective that time has built, showing readiness not to judge past mistakes or achievements but to integrate them and move forward to the next stage. When this card appears, it can be read as a sign that it is now time to respond to a decision you have been putting off, or to a call from deep within.
judgement.reversed: When Judgement appears reversed, it indicates a state of still hesitating even after hearing the signal of awakening ringing within, or clinging to the old framework out of fear of change. Like lying still in a coffin without having heard the trumpet's call, self-criticism or regret over past matters may be eroding the strength needed to move forward. Sometimes this also appears as reaching a hasty conclusion before being truly ready, or ignoring one's genuine calling while being swayed by others' judgments. During this time, rather than forcing an answer, it is necessary to first look inward at what is holding you back.
judgement.love: In relationships, this card shows that an opportunity has arrived to resolve old misunderstandings or conflicts and to see each other with new eyes. Rather than covering up past wounds, it may be time to bring them out honestly for reconciliation, or to redefine the relationship itself. For those who are single, it carries the message of looking back on past relationship patterns to reconfirm what form of love you truly want.
judgement.career: In work and career, this signifies a point where your efforts and career so far are being evaluated as a kind of reckoning, or a period when an inner conviction to change direction grows stronger. A long-postponed decision to change jobs, switch fields of study, or take on a new challenge may come into clearer focus. As Judgement has appeared, it is important to ask yourself—not by others' standards, but your own—what your true calling and talents are, and to respond to that question.
judgement.money: Financially, this suggests it is time to look back on past spending habits or investment approaches and settle accounts. It can be a good opportunity to sort out long-neglected financial issues, debts, or contractual matters while establishing a new financial plan. Rather than expecting a sudden drastic change, real improvement begins with a sober evaluation of the patterns you've followed so far.
judgement.advice: The first step is to be honest with the voice calling from deep within you right now. Without denying the past, accept it as it is, but find the courage to use that experience as a stepping stone toward the next stage. It is fine not to have complete certainty—just try to respond, even in small ways, to the call you feel right now.

temperance.name: Temperance
temperance.meaning: This card symbolizes balance, patience, and harmonious integration. The key is finding the right timing that fits the natural flow, rather than rushing. It represents the ability to gently reconcile opposing energies, and the best outcomes come from avoiding extremes and walking the middle path. Right now, a process of slowly finding balance, step by step, is needed.
temperance.sym_person: A winged angel stands with one foot on land and one in water, pouring water between two cups
temperance.sym_symbol: Two cups, a white robe marked with a triangle symbol, a golden crown, iris flowers
temperance.sym_bg: A clear pond and a golden sky
temperance.upright: The angel, standing with one foot on land and one in water while transferring water between two cups, demonstrates the ability to move between two different realms and maintain balance. When this card appears, it signals that now is a time for coordinating and blending both sides rather than making extreme choices. Just as water flows naturally from one side to the other, things proceed smoothly when you respect the proper flow and timing rather than forcing an outcome. The golden sky and calm pond are a scene that only becomes visible when impatience is set aside and one waits calmly, telling us that patience is not in vain. This card carries a message of integration—that elements which seem to oppose each other, such as reason and emotion, work and rest, or your position and the other person's, can actually move together within a single flow.
temperance.reversed: Reversed, Temperance brings to mind water spilling or overflowing from one cup, read as a warning that balance is breaking down. There is a risk that rushing to produce results, or conversely holding back too much, could cause emotions or circumstances to burst out. It may be worth examining situations where forcing two different things together ends up losing both, or where a flow is tipping toward excess. This is a time to slow down and reflect on where the balance has been lost.
temperance.love: If two people are relating to each other at different speeds and intensities, now is a time to acknowledge that difference and gradually find alignment. Rather than pushing forward, listening to the other person's rhythm and sharing your heart little by little, like pouring water between cups, can help the relationship deepen steadily. In a relationship facing conflict, true reconciliation begins not from one side winning, but from the point where both sides give a little ground.
temperance.career: At work, a situation is emerging where you need to balance multiple roles or projects, and a step-by-step approach to coordination will yield better results than overextending yourself. In collaborating with colleagues or superiors, flexibility in blending different styles is needed rather than insisting on your own way. An attitude of steady accumulation rather than rushing for results will build a more stable position in the long run.
temperance.money: A distribution that avoids extremes between spending and saving, or investment and safe assets, will help your current financial flow. Rather than making major decisions hastily, weighing several options and adjusting gradually will bring more stable results. A long-term, balanced plan rather than immediate gain may ultimately lead to greater stability.
temperance.advice: Rather than forcing two different feelings or options within you into one, try moving gently between them like the angel, with a foot on each side. Respecting the natural pace at which things flow, rather than rushing the outcome, is the attitude needed right now. When you avoid extremes and walk the middle path, a more harmonious ending than expected may be waiting for you.

five-of-swords.name: Five of Swords
five-of-swords.meaning: This card symbolizes conflict, the emptiness of victory, and moral compromise. It represents a hollow win where you may triumph but lose something important in the process. It's worth considering the cost of achieving results by any means necessary. Even if you've gained something now, take a look at what may have been lost along the way.
five-of-swords.sym_person: A man holding three swords with a triumphant smile, while two figures walk away in the background
five-of-swords.sym_bg: A coastline with clouds remaining after a storm
five-of-swords.upright: On a shore where the storm has just passed, a man clutching three swords is smiling, but the backs of the two figures walking away from him reveal that this victory is far from complete. This card suggests that even if you've achieved the outcome you wanted in an argument or dispute, trust or relationships may have quietly crumbled in the process. When you focus too much on defeating an opponent or protecting your pride, there comes a moment when you lose sight of the person or value you should have protected instead. It's worth reconsidering whether what you now hold in your hands is a true victory, or merely a sword left behind in a place others have abandoned. What matters more than the conflict itself is how you chose to resolve it—and that choice becomes the key to determining the future of your relationships.
five-of-swords.reversed: Reversed, this card can indicate a movement away from a prolonged dispute and toward finding a path to reconciliation. This is a period when attempts begin to set aside the arrogance of having won, reflect on your own attitude, and work to restore the relationship. Sometimes the wounds from past conflicts haven't fully healed yet, making apologies or reconciliation feel awkward or clumsy. Rather than determining who won or lost, the effort to understand each other's perspective is what has the power to change this card's direction.
